contents: # Widget (uhifadhi/widget-module) — the dashboard machinery: the registry
# modules declare their surfaces into, the layouts each person adopted, and the
# library component that arranges them.
# THERE IS NOTHING TO CONFIGURE, and that is why this file has no `widget:` key.
# Which widgets a dashboard ships, what they are called, which headed section
# the library files them under and how wide each may sit are the DECLARING
# MODULE's to say — a module writes a WidgetSurfaceInterface and tags it. A
# second place to say the same things would be a second place for the two to
# disagree, and a key here would be that second place.
# THE BUNDLE ALSO NEEDS NO DOCTRINE BLOCK. It maps its own entities, so
# `widget_preference` and `widget_custom_preset` arrive without a mappings key
# in this project.
# WHAT THIS FILE IS FOR is the one line below, which the recipe cannot write for
# you.
# THE ONE LINE THIS RECIPE CANNOT WRITE — and it is REQUIRED, not an extra you
# add later.
# A stored layout belongs to a PERSON, and the accounts of an installation are
# not this bundle's. So the bundle maps that association to an interface that
# uhifadhi/module-contracts publishes, and you resolve the interface to your own
# class. A recipe has no way to know what you call your people, or whether you
# have an account class yet.
# HOW FAR YOU GET WITHOUT IT — honestly. The bundle installs, the container
# compiles, and the kernel boots. What you CANNOT do is touch the schema.
# Anything that walks the metadata — `doctrine:schema:create`,
# `doctrine:schema:update`, `doctrine:migrations:diff` — stops on the unresolved
# interface:
#   In MappingException.php line 72:
#     Class 'Uhifadhi\ModuleContracts\Entity\UserInterface' does not exist
# That is not a bug to route around. Both tables carry a NOT NULL foreign key to
# a person; a layout with no owner is not half a layout.
# IF YOU INSTALLED uhifadhi/team-module THERE IS NOTHING TO DO. Team provides the
# account class, so team states the resolution from its own bundle (0.3.2 and
# later) and this whole step is already answered:
#   doctrine:
#       orm:
#           resolve_target_entities:
#               Uhifadhi\ModuleContracts\Entity\UserInterface: Uhifadhi\Team\Entity\User
# You do not write that. It is here so you can recognise it in `debug:config
# doctrine` and know where it came from.
# OTHERWISE — no team, or an account class of your own — IT IS YOURS, and it is
# one line naming your class instead. It has to answer the contract's seven
# questions — getId, getUuidString, getEmail, getFirstName, getLastName,
# getFullName, getRangerCode — and be in the mapping chain; a project created
# from the uhifadhi skeleton keeps its entities under the stock Symfony root,
# which the doctrine-bundle recipe's own prefix already covers.
#   doctrine:
#       orm:
#           resolve_target_entities:
#               Uhifadhi\ModuleContracts\Entity\UserInterface: App\Entity\Person
# YOUR ANSWER WINS EVEN WITH TEAM INSTALLED. Team's is prepended, and prepended
# configuration loses to the application's — so naming your own class is all it
# takes, and there is nothing to disable first.
# MERGE IT INTO THE BLOCK ALREADY THERE. config/packages/doctrine.yaml opens
# with `doctrine:`, and a second `doctrine:` key in the same file is not valid
# YAML — Symfony refuses to boot with `Duplicate key "doctrine" detected`. The
# `resolve_target_entities` key goes under the `orm:` that is already in that
# file, beside `mappings`.
# Write it ONCE. resolve_target_entities is one map, so the seam's AreaInterface
# line and this one sit side by side under it, and a module installed later that
# points at a person needs nothing further. The seam's line is ALWAYS yours:
# only your installation knows what it calls an area, so no package can answer
# that one for you — which is exactly the test for whether a step belongs to the
# installation or to the package.
# THEN, in this order:
#   bin/console doctrine:migrations:diff      # your history, your migration
#   bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate
# The bundle ships entities, not migrations: the tables are the bundle's, but the
# migration history is yours, and a vendor replaying its own versions into it
# would fight every `diff` you ever run.
# UNINSTALLING A MODULE LEAVES ITS LAYOUTS BEHIND, on purpose. Rows are keyed by
# a surface string, nothing reads a surface no module claims, and reinstalling
# gives everybody the dashboard they had. Deliberate cleanup is a command you
# run, never something that happens to you:
#   bin/console widget:prune --dry-run
